title: Before You Share That Claim, Ask These 3 Questions

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Before you send that post, give it three questions.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: One: where did the claim start? Not who reposted it. Find the original document, interview, or report—and check the date.
scenes.on_screen: 1. WHERE DID IT START? FIND ORIGINAL

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Two: what does the evidence actually prove? A logo can show certification. A company filing can show ownership. Neither gives you permission to invent extra claims.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: Three: did the post jump from one person’s actions to blaming Jewish people as a group? That jump needs challenging, not another share.
scenes.on_screen: 3. DID IT JUMP TO GROUP BLAME?

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Then check a reliable independent source. And if the answer is still unclear, saying “I don’t know yet” is better than confidently spreading something false.
scenes.on_screen: CHECK INDEPENDENT SOURCE · IT'S OK TO SAY 'NOT SURE'

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: You don’t have to win every comment section. You can be the person who brings the actual source.
scenes.on_screen: BE THE PERSON WHO BRINGS THE SOURCE

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Which claim should we check next? Specific claims. Real evidence.
scenes.source: Beyond the Myth · Facts, not scapegoats
